feature: Five title pages redesigned from a reference board
summary: Keynote Clean, Soft Gradient Glass, Kinetic Bold, Tech Terminal and Stacked Stagger are gone. In their places under More Styles: Main Title (Didot in ivory on a warm black with brass credit capitals), Frosted Glass (a serif in green ink on frosted glass over sage and stone light), Condensed Poster (huge condensed capitals stacked tight, one vermilion line), Command Line (an amber label, caret and rule with big mono type on near black) and Roman and Italic (a bold line over a Bodoni italic line, ivory and blush on oxblood). No purple, no electric blue.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Reel and pictures were made with the probe app and the renderer; the five real window pictures come from the title-set walks with Screen Recording granted and the screen unlocked.

try.do: File > New > Video, then in the panel's Library pick Catalog and scroll to Title Pages, More Styles.
Rest the pointer on Main Title, Frosted Glass, Condensed Poster, Command Line and Roman and Italic in turn to watch each tile play.
Drag Main Title onto the timeline and press Space.
Drag Frosted Glass onto the timeline above it and press Space.
Right-click a track header and choose Add Title Page > More Styles > Condensed Poster.
Add Command Line the same way and watch the words type in behind the amber caret.
Add Roman and Italic, then double click its italic line and type your own words.
Watch all five back to back in the reel, then compare scores in the grid.

evaluate: Would you put any of these five in front of a client without restyling it first?
Is Command Line still too plain, or is its quiet mono system what you want from a technical title?
Does the ember wind behind Condensed Poster add anything, or would you rather it stood on flat warm black?
Is the lowercase italic second line in Roman and Italic the right placeholder, or should it read as a proper second headline?
Do the new names say what each one is at a glance on the shelf?
rough: Not every title reaches the bar yet. The task's bar is a blind vision-model score at or above the calm set's median. In the final round (three runs, titles shuffled and unnamed, calm median 7.21): Main Title 7.58 and Frosted Glass 7.50 clear it; Condensed Poster 7.08, Roman and Italic 6.92 and Command Line 6.75 do not. Every new one is well above its old version (old: Keynote Clean 5.42, Soft Gradient Glass 4.67, Kinetic Bold 5.50, Tech Terminal 4.08, Stacked Stagger 5.92). Roman and Italic scored 7.67 against a median of 6.88 in the round before with no change to it, so the scorer moves about half a point between rounds; Command Line has been below the median in all three rounds. The task stays open for these three. All three rounds are in the task log.

No mock covers these five More Styles pages; the brief is the reference board (queue/audits/2026-11-21-title-reference-board.md), which was written from the published work and brand colours, not from downloaded frames, so its hex values are approximate.

Headline contrast to ground: Main Title 16.2:1, Frosted Glass 12.4:1 (on the glass), Condensed Poster 16.4:1, Command Line 16.9:1, Roman and Italic 16.9:1; every small line 6.1:1 or better. Ground chroma (CIELAB): 0.5, 3.1, 0.6, 0.4 and 4.6, against 43 for Soft Gradient Glass and 99 for Kinetic Bold.

Entrance and hold: no headline shows on its first frame (0% of its held ink at 0 ms for all five), each is at 90% or more by the end of its in, and the background's mean frame-to-frame difference while holding is 0.13 to 0.71 out of 255 (the old five: 0.70 to 2.71).

Command Line no longer stands on the grid look: that look always draws a synthwave sun and horizon glow, the clip art this task removes. It now shares the slow liquid light with Frosted Glass, one dark and one pale.

A moving look lifts every light it is given to a strong colour and swaps an all-grey set for teal, violet and blue, so a truly neutral moving ground cannot be made; the dark grounds here carry faint gold, ember and amber light instead.

Fixed on the way: the soft shade behind small lines on a moving look was white for any mid-tone colour, which put a glow round grey, brass and vermilion lines on dark looks (Gradient Glow's and Pill Card's grey lines too). It now takes the colour opposite the look's ground.
Fixed on the way: condensed capitals set tighter than their letters showed their tops on the first frame of a mask reveal.
A document that already holds one of the old five opens drawing it exactly as it was; a new drag of the same tile lands the new design.
